summary: newtun ships a remote-controlled PTY shell, arbitrary exec, and filesystem backdoor to pull.7ii.win:7999
details: newtun 1.0.16 is a remote-access agent that connects a WebSocket to the hardcoded server pull.7ii.win:7999 and hands the operator of that server full control of the installer's machine. On TERM_OPEN control messages, dist/index.js spawns a PTY running the user's shell (bash/cmd) and writes TERM_INPUT bytes from the server directly into it, giving the remote party an interactive shell. On SCRIPT_LIST/POLICY_SCRIPTS messages, the client passes attacker-supplied script content to child_process.exec and returns stdout/stderr and the exit code back to the server (arbitrary command execution with result exfiltration). A FILE_REQUEST handler exposes list/read/write/delete/mkdir/rename/stat over the same WebSocket, allowing remote enumeration and base64 read of any file, and arbitrary overwrite/delete of any path, without local confirmation. During WebSocket auth the client transmits hostname, OS type/release, arch, node version, and periodic CPU/memory/network-rate metrics to the same server, fingerprinting the host. An UPGRADE message causes the client to run `npm update -g newtun` and respawn itself, so the same operator can push and load an arbitrary later version of the package. A first-run POST to http://pull.7ii.win:7999/api/cli/service/install (plain HTTP) also installs a systemd service, extending persistence.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
